title: Renovation eviction by-law and short-term rentals
subtitle: Rockway Centre kitchen options, King Street West rezoning, school safety, public trees, KIRC operations and streetlight outages
overview: Council's last meeting before the summer break moved ahead on work toward a rental renovation licensing by-law. Staff will refer education and support measures to the Housing for All update and report back on a draft licensing by-law by the end of the first quarter of 2026 {{vote:m4}}. Council also chose to take no action on city licensing of short-term rentals {{vote:m5}}, so no licensing regime will be created for now.

Other decisions affect daily life in the city. Council approved a rezoning for 924-944 King Street West, adopted a new Public Tree By-law, and set school-zone speed limits, no-stopping rules and crossing guards for growing neighbourhoods. It approved the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex operating model and told staff to proceed with the Rockway Centre replacement, with kitchen options to be priced separately. It also asked staff to work with Enova Power Corp. on better communication about streetlight outages.

Council upheld the prohibited-dog designations in two appeals, approved brownfield tax grants for two downtown properties and appointed an Artist in Residence. The Mayor announced $10 million in provincial funding for a quad-gymnasium at the indoor recreation complex, which is expected to open in August 2026.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to refer education and support measures to the Housing for All update, pursue funding, press the Province to enact the bad-faith eviction rules in Bill 97, and report back on a draft rental renovation licensing by-law, with costs and staffing, by the end of Q1 2026.

Council took no action on city licensing of short-term rentals, citing existing platform regulation, the cost of a licensing program, and the ability to handle noise and other concerns through current by-laws.
Staff will proceed to Phase 3 and issue a request for proposals for a new older adult centre within 1.5 kilometres of the current site, with kitchen options priced separately.
Council approved the zoning by-law amendment and adopted the Urban Design Brief for the property.
Council approved the staffing and financial operating model for the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex and directed that its impacts be built into the 2026 and 2027 budgets.
Council repealed and replaced the Public Tree By-law, approved related administrative penalties and directed staff to implement education, enforcement and monitoring.
Council approved lower speed limits, no-stopping zones, a school bus loading zone and crossing guard changes near schools in several growing neighbourhoods.
Council directed staff to work with Enova Power Corp. on better communication, resident updates and service levels for streetlight outages.

debate: Delegates supporting a renovation licensing by-law described bad-faith evictions, hidden homelessness and the burden on tenants of fighting cases at the Landlord and Tenant Board. They argued the province is slow to act and that other Ontario cities are moving ahead.

Councillors opposed to the renovation by-law said it cannot stop a notice from being issued or regulate landlord behaviour. They also questioned the lack of data on whether Hamilton's by-law works and said the Tribunal already penalizes bad actors. Supporters called it one more tool that adds accountability and may reduce Tribunal cases.

Staff said the consultant cost for the renovation by-law was an upper estimate, and that similar licensing programs elsewhere do not fully cover their own costs. The Mayor asked that the consultant not simply be sole-sourced.

On short-term rentals, a host delegate said commercial insurance and licence fees would push out small local hosts and proposed a simple registration system instead. Staff said commercial insurance would not be required and an inexpensive option for the city's additional-insured requirement was available. Councillors favouring no action cited few complaints, cost, and over-regulation. Others said short-term rentals are businesses and should be licensed.

On the Rockway Centre, staff said engagement favoured a warming kitchen and existing commercial kitchens are lightly used. One councillor questioned adding a costly kitchen without a business case. The Mayor and another councillor noted that the current centre has a commercial kitchen and that groups seek kitchen space. Council settled on pricing all options separately.
